description.narrative:
The overall goal of the SCII project is: The resilience of communities, institutions and ecosystems in the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) region enhanced. Phase 2 of the SCII project will address the following outcome areas:
Outcome 1: Optimized Implementation of IDDRSI Consolidated.
Outcome 2. Analytical Capacities and Institutional Mechanisms for Food Security, Nutrition Information and Resilience Building in the IGAD Region Strengthened.

Syftet med detta bidrag är att konsolidera genomförandet av IGAD´s Initiativ för motståndskraft mot torkkatastrofer och hållbarhets genom att fortsatt stärka den kapaciteten i medlemsstaternas institutioner i deras utveckling av resultatbaserade system och i dess genomförande där planering, övervakning, utvärdering, finansiering och rapportering är överensstämmer och är resultatorienterad. I användandet av resultaten av denna insats så ska IGAD stärka sin analytiska kapacitet och institutionella mekanism för livsmedelssäkerhet, näringsupplysning och byggande av motståndskraft i regionen.

The purpose of this contribution is to consolidate implementation of IGAD Drought Disaster Resilience & Sustainability Initiative through further strengthening the institutional capacity of IGAD Member State institutions to develop a result-based management system where planning, monitoring, evaluation, budgeting and reporting are coherent and result oriented. In addition, IGAD will also strengthen analytical capacities and institutional mechanisms for Food Security, Nutrition Information and Resilience Building in the IGAD Region.

sector.narrative: Food security policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The year 2023 is the first year of implementation of the contribution (01 April 2023 to 31st March 2024). During the reporting period all planned activities accomplished as per the work plan approved during the signing of the agreement except the activities planned for Sudan due to the internal conflict. IGAD submitted the year 1 annual reports of the Strengthening Coordination and Implementation of IDDRSI (IGAD Drought Disaster Resilience and Sustainability Initiative), both the narrative and financial reports, on time as per the due date indicated in the cooperation agreement. Both reports were clear and comprehensive.
The optimized implementation of the IGAD Drought Disaster Resilience and Sustainability Initiative (IDDRSI) relies on enhancing institutional capacities within Member State institutions. Sweden has been supporting the initiative since 2018 in two successive phases.
Phase 1 of the Support to the IDDRSI Coordination Unit primarily focuses on building the capacity of the unit and the Country Programmes Implementation units on a Result-Based Management System and establishment of the Country Programme Papers (CPPs) in all IGAD member states. The follow up support during the phase 2 of the project was designed to address these deficiencies and enhance the result-based management systems in countries that faced challenges during Phase 1 targeted to strengthen institutional capacities, ensuring a more coherent, result-oriented, and impactful implementation of the IDDRSI.
Similarly, the third phase of support relies on experiences gained from the previous two rounds of support from Sweden, where establishing National Experts Panels (NEPs), which provide technical support to the National IDDRSI Steering Committees has been given a priority. Accordingly, NEPs have made significant progress in various areas across the IGAD region, including reviewing Country Programming Papers and projects, compiling programming documents, sharing information on new projects, and enhancing understanding of resilience-building initiatives.
Key achievements during the reporting period are the following.
Strengthened result-based management system established for CPPs and hence CPPs have now developed clear objectives, targets, and outcomes aligned with IDDRSI goals and national development priorities.
Comprehensive Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) frameworks established, along with baseline data, data collection and management procedures, reporting mechanisms, risk management strategies, and adaptive management principles.
The National Expert Panels (NEPs) established within the IDDRSI framework are now becoming crucial in ensuring effective coordination and implementation of IDDRSI projects across member states. They provide technical advice, facilitate monitoring, collect sectoral data, and generate reports, among other responsibilities.
Successive National Expert Panel (NEP) meetings conducted and provided technical support to the National Country Program Papers (CPPs).
IGAD Food Security Nutrition and Resilience Analysis Hub (IFRAH) collaborated with other IGAD programs, divisions, specialized institutions, member states, and partners strengthened to generate and disseminate timely information on food security, nutrition, and resilience.
Timely production and dissemination of decision-support products, including monthly FSNWG statements and early warning reports on forecasted El Niño conditions, for proactive actions.
IFRAH trained national staff to strengthen their analytical capacities in food security and nutrition analyses, facilitated bi-annual meetings on these topics, and hosted a high-level dialogue event on enhancing food security in the IGAD region.
IGAD Climate Prediction and Application Center (ICPAC) is now playing a pivotal role in disseminating climate information through the Greater Horn of Africa Climate Outlook Forum (GHACOF), focusing on Eastern Africa. This forum provided a platform for stakeholders to develop scenarios and anticipate actions before the start of the rainy season, given the prevailing El Niño conditions and positive Indian Ocean Dipole.
Uganda conducted the CPPs Steering Committees at the national and sub-national levels. Other countries planned the CPPs Steering Committee meetings in the month of October. Arrangements to implement activities were made by harmonizing the merger of the IDDRSI Program Coordination Unite with the Planning, Coordination and Partnership Division of IGAD.
The IDDRSI Regional Staff have provided coordination support to regional projects including resource mobilization. The National IDDRSI Coordinators contributed to the resilience programming, coordination, knowledge management, and early warning information systems.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
